open_points.subject: connection validation timing
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: Which actions count as using the photo folder: connecting, confirming, listing deliverables, placing a photo, or some combination of them?
options: refuse the connection immediately
allow connection and confirmation but refuse listing
allow listing but refuse placement
check at every folder access
open_points.default_guess: allow the connection record, then check and refuse at every operation that accesses the folder

witness.initial: An owner connects a photo folder that is already linked outside the root.
events: The owner connects and confirms it through the agent.
The owner asks to see what can be delivered.
outcomes: Connection is refused because validation during connection counts as use.
Connection is stored and confirmed; the later delivery query is refused because that is the first use.

open_points.subject: confirmed connection state
open_points.text: a connection record the owner has confirmed; delivery becomes possible for that project
open_points.question: May a connection whose photo folder currently links outside the root be stored or confirmed despite delivery being refused when the folder is used, and if so does a later refusal invalidate that connection?
options: do not store the connection
store it but prohibit confirmation
store and confirm it while retaining that state after refusal
invalidate or revoke it when the outside link is discovered
open_points.default_guess: store and confirm it, refuse the use, and retain the connection so it can work after the folder is repaired

witness.initial: A confirmed connection points to a photo folder linked outside its root.
events: The agent detects the outside link and refuses the request.
The owner repairs the link and tries again.
outcomes: The connection remains confirmed and the retry succeeds.
Detection invalidates the connection and the owner must reconnect or reconfirm.

open_points.subject: subfolder containment
open_points.text: a connection whose subfolder is written to leave its root is refused
open_points.question: What exact written subfolder forms count as leaving the root, and is containment decided before or after path normalization?
options: reject only normalized parent traversal outside the root
also reject absolute paths and platform-specific separators
reject any parent-traversal component even when normalization remains inside
apply filesystem-specific case, drive and Unicode rules
open_points.default_guess: parse with the target platform's path rules, reject absolute paths, normalize dot components, and require the normalized result to remain beneath the root

witness.initial: The root is /project and the submitted subfolder is photos/../photos.
events: The owner submits the connection through the agent.
outcomes: The connection is accepted because the normalized path stays under /project.
The connection is refused because the written value contains a parent-traversal component.

open_points.subject: linked-folder containment
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root
open_points.question: Which indirections make a photo folder 'linked outside': the final folder being a symbolic link, a link in any ancestor, hard links, junctions, bind mounts, or a root that is itself linked elsewhere; and against which canonical root is 'outside' measured?
options: resolve symbolic links only at the final folder
resolve every path component against the root's canonical target
also treat junctions and mount indirections as links
apply the rule only to the configured photo-folder entry
open_points.default_guess: resolve the root and every component of the photo-folder path canonically and refuse any resolved target outside the canonical root, including platform-equivalent directory links

open_points.subject: scope of linked-folder rule
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: Does outside-root link protection apply only to the photo folder, or also to the root itself and every other connected folder used by the project?
options: photo folder only
all connected folders
photo folder and every ancestor including the root
open_points.default_guess: apply the same containment rule to every connected folder and ancestor used for delivery

witness.initial: The photo subfolder is ordinary, but the configured root itself is a link to a location outside the apparent root path.
events: The owner connects and confirms the project.
The agent reads the photo folder.
outcomes: Access succeeds because only the photo folder entry is checked for being a link.
Access is refused because the root or an ancestor resolves outside the trusted boundary.
witness.observer: the owner and the operator responsible for folder isolation

open_points.subject: outside-link refusal result
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: What is refused and what observable result is returned: the whole project operation, the affected folder, or individual files, and what status or reason does the owner receive?
options: fail the whole operation with a connection error
report every affected file as rejected with an outside-root reason
omit inaccessible files and continue
disable delivery for the project
open_points.default_guess: fail the whole folder-dependent operation with an explicit outside-root-folder reason and return no partial file list or placements

witness.initial: A project has one normal photo folder and one photo-folder path that resolves outside the root.
events: The owner asks to see what can be delivered.
outcomes: The entire request is refused and returns no file statuses.
Files from the normal folder are returned while files under the outside link are individually rejected.

open_points.subject: refusal side effects
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: When the outside link is discovered during listing or placement, which records or files, if any, may already have been written, and must the operation leave everything unchanged?
options: perform no writes for the whole operation
retain writes completed before discovery
roll back Portal-store writes but retain diagnostics
change the connection state while leaving delivery data unchanged
open_points.default_guess: detect containment before any read or write for that folder and leave connection, delivery and Portal data unchanged on refusal

witness.initial: Two chosen photos are being placed; the first is under the root and the second is reached through an outside link.
events: The owner requests placement of both photos.
The agent processes the first photo and then discovers the outside link for the second.
outcomes: Nothing is placed because the request is rejected before writes.
The first photo remains placed and only the second is refused.
witness.observer: the owner and the calling flow

open_points.subject: link changes during use
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: If the folder or an ancestor changes into an outside-root link after validation or while an operation is running, at what point must the operation refuse access and what happens to work already completed?
options: check once at the start of each action
check separately before every file access
use handles that remain confined to the validated root
allow the current action and detect the change next time
open_points.default_guess: open and access files through root-confined handles, refusing any access whose resolved target escapes even if links change during the operation

witness.initial: The photo folder resolves inside the root when delivery is scanned.
events: The agent reports a file as ready.
Another process replaces an ancestor with a link outside the root.
The owner asks the agent to place the ready file.
outcomes: Placement is refused because containment is rechecked at access time.
Placement reads and stores the outside file because the earlier scan's validation is reused.
witness.observer: the owner and the operator responsible for folder isolation

open_points.subject: failure reason precedence
open_points.text: a photo folder linked outside the root is refused when it is used
open_points.question: When an outside link also makes the folder unavailable or makes a selected file differ from the scanned file, which promised failure and reason takes precedence?
options: outside-root refusal takes precedence
unavailable-folder refusal takes precedence
changed-file refusal takes precedence
return every applicable reason
open_points.default_guess: outside-root refusal takes precedence because it is the trust-boundary failure and no file content should be examined further

witness.initial: A scanned file was inside the root; before placement its folder is replaced by an outside link whose target contains different content at the same path.
events: The owner requests placement of the previously scanned file.
The agent detects both the changed content and the outside-root resolution.
outcomes: The file is refused as an outside-root folder violation.
The file is reported only as changed since scanning.
